title: AU Microscopii: TESS sector 1 light curve (a spotted, flaring M dwarf)
credit: TESS, sector 1 (NASA; SPOC light curve from MAST)

license.statement: NASA mission data, released through MAST without restriction on reuse. MAST asks that work using its data acknowledge the mission and the archive.

columns.name: flux error
columns.description: PDCSAP error over the median, one sigma

masks.rule: any nonzero flag drops the cadence

reductions: Every kept two-minute cadence is stored with its own time stamp; nothing is averaged.
Flux is stored to 20 ppm, its error to 1 ppm and time to 0.00001 d (0.86 s); the manifest records the largest rounding.

AU Mic is a young, active M1 dwarf in the Beta Pictoris moving group with strong spot modulation and frequent flares; Gilbert et al. (2022) find 48 flares in 25.07 d of this sector at 2-minute cadence with their own pipeline.

source.archive: MAST (Barbara A. Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes)

citations.text: TESS Light Curves - All Sectors, STScI/MAST

steps: Read TIME, PDCSAP_FLUX, PDCSAP_FLUX_ERR and QUALITY from the LIGHTCURVE binary table.
Keep cadences with QUALITY 0 and a finite time, flux and error.
Divide flux and error by the median kept flux.
Store time, flux and error as table-columns/1.

assumptions: PDCSAP flux has had instrumental systematics and crowding removed by SPOC; that correction is used as published.
Times are barycentric dynamical time for the target, as SPOC corrects them.
The light is the TESS band (600 to 1000 nm). The star has a transiting planet whose transits are shallower than the flares and are not removed.

validation.check: a period search and a four-harmonic refinement find the published period within its stated uncertainty (0.03 d)

against.ref: Gilbert et al. 2022, AJ 163, 147 (4.85 +- 0.03 d from all TESS sectors)
